---
applyTo: "app/models/**/*.rb"
---

# Models

- Group model declarations under comment headings in this order: `### Scopes ###`, `### Constants ###`, `### Attributes ###`, `### Enumerations ###`, `### Associations ###`, `### Validations ###`, `### Callbacks ###`, `### Modules (GemName) ###`, `### Public Methods ###`. Leave out a group if the model has nothing in it.
- Name the gem in brackets in the modules heading, e.g. `### Modules (FriendlyId) ###` above `extend FriendlyId`.
- Give each gem its own modules heading, in alphabetical order unless one gem needs to be set up before another, e.g. `### Modules (Devise) ###` then `### Modules (FriendlyId) ###`.
- Put an `include` or `extend` at the top of the model only when a later declaration needs it, e.g. a macro it defines or a callback that needs to run first. Leave out the heading and add a comment saying what needs it, e.g. `# Sluggable must come before slug_from` above `include Sluggable`.
- Put shared logic in `concerning` blocks. Put a block that supports a gem's module under that module's heading, e.g. `concerning :Slugs` under `### Modules (FriendlyId) ###`. Put other blocks under `### Public Methods ###`, e.g. `concerning :Publishing`, except that `concerning :UserAccess` MAY go at the top of the model.
- Put private methods last, after `private`. Order them by the group they support, in the same order as the headings, e.g. a method for `validate :published_at_cannot_be_in_the_future` before a method for `before_save :set_published_at`.
- When an attribute has `presence: true`, add `allow_blank: true` to its other validators, so a blank value only gets "can't be blank", e.g. `validates :title, presence: true, length: { maximum: TITLE_MAX_LENGTH, allow_blank: true }`.
- Tidy values with `normalizes` under `### Attributes ###`, e.g. `normalizes :isbn, with: ->(isbn) { isbn.delete("-") }`. You MUST NOT tidy a value in a `before_validation` callback or an overridden writer, except before Rails 7.1, which has no `normalizes`: then use `before_validation { self.title = title&.strip }` under `### Callbacks ###`.
- Always pass `dependent:` to every `has_many`. Use `dependent: :restrict_with_exception` unless you know what happens to the associated records, e.g. `has_many :publications, dependent: :restrict_with_exception`, and use another value only once that is decided, e.g. `has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy`. Write `dependent: nil` only when the records stay, e.g. for a scoped association another association already handles, e.g. `has_many :approved_comments, -> { approved }, class_name: "Comment", dependent: nil`. You MUST NOT leave the option out.
- When code outside the model builds a query on a record's association in more than one step, give the model a method that returns the query, e.g. `def unlocked_comments = comments.where(locked: false)` on `Post`. Keep the method to reads, and leave writes to the caller, e.g. `post.unlocked_comments.update_all(locked: true, updated_at: Time.zone.now)`. When only one task uses the method, put it in a `concerning` block named after that task under `### Public Methods ###`, e.g. `concerning :Archiving`, and move it out of the block when another task needs it.
- The read method MAY use a scope on the associated model, e.g. `scope :unlocked, -> { where(locked: false) }` on `Comment` and `def unlocked_comments = comments.unlocked` on `Post`. Callers still call the method, e.g. `post.unlocked_comments`, not the scope through the association, e.g. `post.comments.unlocked`.
- For a query that starts from a class, give that class a method that builds it, e.g. `def on_posts(posts) = where(post: posts)` in a `class_methods` block on `Comment`, so callers write `Comment.on_posts(posts)`, not `Comment.where(post: posts)`.
- Give each role a user can hold on one record a `user_is_<role>?(user)` method and a `for_user_as_<role>(user)` scope in a `concerning :UserAccess` block, e.g. `def user_is_author?(user)` and `scope :for_user_as_author, ->(user) { where(author_id: user.id) }` in the block's `included` block on `Post`. Keep a role on the whole app on `User` when it covers every record, e.g. `user.app_admin?`. When it only covers some records, give it `UserAccess` methods with the condition, e.g. `def user_is_copy_editor?(user) = draft? && user.copy_editor?` and `scope :for_user_as_copy_editor, ->(user) { user.copy_editor? ? draft : none }`. Put the block under `### Public Methods ###`. It MAY go at the top of the model instead, above `### Scopes ###` and every other heading. Follow where the app's other models put it.
- In `user_is_<role>?`, compare the foreign key for a role from a `belongs_to`, e.g. `author_id == user.id`, and read the record's join rows with `any?` and a block for a role from a join, e.g. `coauthorships.any? { |coauthorship| coauthorship.user_id == user.id }`. You SHOULD NOT compare the records, e.g. `author == user`, or call `include?` or `exists?` on an association, e.g. `coauthors.include?(user)` or `user.coauthored_posts.include?(self)`. In `for_user_as_<role>`, filter the same way, e.g. `where(author_id: user.id)` and `where(id: user.coauthored_posts)`.
- Use callbacks only to change the record's own attributes, e.g. `before_save :set_published_at, if: :published?`. You MUST NOT create, change or delete another record, enqueue a job, send an email or call another service from a callback, including `after_commit` callbacks. Do that work in the form, action or job that does the task, e.g. `NotifySubscribersJob.perform_later(post)` in `PublishPostForm#submit`. See https://bmorrall.github.io/happy_rails/patterns/side-effects-of-saving/ for where each kind of work goes. `dependent:` on an association is allowed, e.g. `has_many :comments, dependent: :destroy`.
- Encrypt a column that stores a secret, e.g. an API key or an access token, with `encrypts` under `### Attributes ###`, e.g. `encrypts :api_key` on `NewsletterServiceIntegration`. You MUST NOT store a secret in a plain column.
- You MUST NOT build or call a service object in a model, e.g. `def client = NewsletterClient.for(self)` or `def sync_newsletter! = NewsletterClient.new.update_list(self)` on a model. Build and call the service in an action that takes the record as an argument, e.g. `NewsletterClient.new.create_newsletter(post)` in `Posts::SendNewsletter#call`.
